claim: WAIT's 'computed cycles == 0 means unbounded' rule is implemented literally on a 16-bit computed timeout, so exponent=3 with an even mantissa (cycles >= 65536, low 16 bits all 0) is treated as an unbounded WAIT and never times out.
spec_ref: docs/isa.md:Opcode table, WAIT row -- "cycles = mantissa << (exponent*5); any encoding whose computed cycles is 0 ... means no timeout ... Otherwise max reach ~1,015,808 cycles (~20.3ms @ 50MHz)" and "Every WAIT writes the shared flag on exit ... 1 if it timed out"

why_survives.directed: Only exponent-0 WAIT timeouts (test_wait_timeout mantissa 5); every other directed WAIT is unbounded (mantissa 0, exponent 0).
why_survives.random: Default generator draws WAIT exponent 0/1 only. wide_timing (--full) rewrites some WAITs to exponent 2/3 with mantissa 1..31, but under its default 50/50 stimulus every such WAIT is met within a few cycles, so whether a 65536+ cycle timeout is armed is never observed; protocol_pins keeps exponent 0/1.
why_survives.board: The only timed WAIT in board firmware is i2c.asm's WAIT SCL,1,T_STRETCH with T_STRETCH = 32768 = 1<<15 (odd mantissa 1), which still fits 16 bits, so the hold_scl_forever timeout still fires.
why_survives.formal: core_wait_props models the timeout correctly, but at BMC depth 20 a timeout target >= 65536 can never be reached, so 'mutant never times out' and 'spec times out at k=65536' are indistinguishable inside the window.
